preview_en:
After the most turbulent week of his time in charge, Michael Carrick is under pressure to deliver a victory for Manchester United as they travel to a Fulham side winless in the Premier League so far.

Match News and Current Form

Álvaro Arbeloa has had an encouraging week despite being the first Fulham boss in seven years to fail to win his first four league games in charge (D1, L3). The Cottagers followed up a spirited 0-0 draw away at Liverpool last week by running out 3-2 winners in a midweek EFL Cup London derby against West Ham. A first league victory of the campaign is top of Arbeloa’s priority list but Fulham’s most noticeable problems predate his tenure, as they’ve suffered a pre-round joint-league high of ten losses since the start of February, while no side has failed to score in more Premier League fixtures than Fulham (ten) this calendar year.

The first six months of Carrick’s Manchester United reign were extremely positive, but a miserable week in which his side were on the wrong end of an incorrect VAR decision to lose the Manchester Derby 1-0 worsened when they blew a two-goal lead to lose 3-2 at home to Brighton in the EFL Cup during the week. For a second season running and just the third time in Premier League history, the Red Devils have accumulated just four points in their opening four games, with their only win coming against newly-promoted Ipswich (5-2). Escaping the ire of a frustrated home support may seem ideal on paper, but a return of just two wins from their last seven away games (D3, L2) highlights United could be in for a tough time wherever they play.

Head-to-Head History

This is arguably United’s favourite matchup, as they’ve won 16 of the last 21 Premier League H2Hs (D4, L1) and are unbeaten on their last ten trips to Craven Cottage (W8, D2).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Fulham have scored 2+ goals in each of their last four competitive home games.

Fulham have won the corner count in seven of their last eight league matches.

United have attempted a pre-round league-high 84 shots this season - their most on record at this stage since 2003/04.

United lost just one of their seven Premier League trips to London last season (W3, D3).

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Gonzalo Garcia has netted each of his last five club and international goals in home matches, with both strikes for Fulham coming after half-time and completing the scoring. No United player has created more chances in the Premier League than Marcus Rashford (nine), and his first goal since returning to the Red Devils could come early since his last four scoring appearances for the club saw him net the match opener.

Fulham’s Ryan Sessegnon is nursing a groin problem, while Luke Shaw has missed United’s last three games but is expected to be nearing a return.

Betting Analysis

United’s troubles make backing Fulham in the double chance market an appealing option.

Author: Ryan Fisher
